description: Na₂Ba(Ge₄O₉)₂ crystallizes in the trigonal P̅3c1 space group. Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.56-2.87 Å. Ba is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to ten O atoms. There are a spread of Ba-O bond distances ranging from 2.74-3.12 Å. There are seven inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to six equivalent O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. All Ge-O bond lengths are 1.93 Å. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two GeO₆ octahedra and corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 53°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.80 Å. In the third Ge site, Ge is bonded to six O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. All Ge-O bond lengths are 1.91 Å. In the fourth Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two GeO₆ octahedra and corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-62°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.81 Å. In the fifth Ge site, Ge is bonded to six O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. There are three shorter (1.88 Å) and three longer (1.91 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the sixth Ge site, Ge is bonded to six equivalent O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. All Ge-O bond lengths are 1.94 Å. In the seventh Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two GeO₆ octahedra and corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 61-62°. There are two shorter (1.77 Å) and two longer (1.82 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. There are nine inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Ba and two Ge atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Ba and two Ge atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Ba and two Ge atoms. In the sixth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na and two Ge atoms to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₂Ge₂ tetrahedra. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Ba and two Ge atoms. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na and two Ge atoms. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one Ba, and two Ge atoms.
